title: JNK India Ltd - 544167 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: JNK India Q2 FY27 revenue rose 3.4% YoY to INR187.5 crores on shipment and monsoon delays; FY27 guidance of 20-25% growth reiterated.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 operating revenue grew 30.4% YoY to INR370.2 crores, but Q2 alone grew only 3.4% to INR187.5 crores as shipment delays and monsoon disruptions deferred roughly INR30-40 crores of dispatches. Q2 EBITDA was INR20.8 crores (11.1% margin) and PAT INR13.3 crores (7.1% margin). Management kept FY27 guidance of 20-25% revenue growth and 12-14% EBITDA margin, leaning on the historical H2-weighted revenue pattern (60-70%). Order wins included a ~INR500 crore export heater package from JNK Global for Nigeria, and the order book stood at INR1,662 crores as of September 30, 2026.

segments.name: Heater / combustion equipment
segments.commentary: Core business; management says heater bid-to-win ratio has been about 30%. Roughly half of the INR5,000 crore pipeline is combustion equipment.

segments.name: Non-heater / non-combustion equipment
segments.commentary: About INR2,500 crores of opportunities, of which ~INR1,000 crores already bid and ~INR1,500 crores to be bid within 1-2 months. Targets include ONGC offshore, a steel company project and NTPC (bid due November 20). Expected bid-to-win 10-15%.

segments.name: JNK Chemdist (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Order book about INR20 crores; focus on green hydrogen, sustainable fuels and chemicals, with meaningful revenue expected in roughly two years. H1 subsidiary revenue was about INR30 crores per analyst's calculation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance maintained: 20-25% operating revenue growth and 12-14% EBITDA margin on operational revenue.
H2 expected to be execution-intensive; H2 historically contributes 60-70% of annual revenue.
Management expects the balance 60-65% of FY27 revenue to be executable within the year; about INR1,500 crores of order book revenue carries into FY28.
Significant pipeline opportunities expected to materialise by end-FY27; order inflow may spill into Q1 FY28.
Dangote/JNK Global balance scope (possible further ~INR500 crores for JNK India) expected in about two to three months, not confirmed.
Kenya refinery inquiries expected in about December; order finalisation expected in four to five months.
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were discussed in the call.
demand_pricing: Export order from JNK Global for a heater package in Nigeria worth ~INR500 crores, 18-month delivery, covering design, engineering, manufacturing, supply and transport. Management called it the largest export order to date and a repeat order.
Two domestic flare package orders aggregating INR30 crores, 16-month execution timeline.
Q2 shipment and monsoon disruptions deferred roughly INR30-40 crores of revenue.
Logistics challenges linked to geopolitical situation and severe monsoon affected fabrication and site erection.

Africa (Nigeria, Kenya, Ethiopia) is a focus area; BPCL Vizag refinery and petrochemical project (~INR5,000 crore opportunity for industry players) is not in the pipeline as BPCL has not formally declared it; tenders expected in 6-8 months.
Management expects October and November to be slow, with recovery in December-March.

qa_highlights.question: What levers support 20-25% growth and margins given weak H1/Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 growth is already about 30%; the company typically books 30-40% of revenue in H1 and 60-65% in H2, and management is confident of both revenue and EBITDA guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the order book is executable in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Balance 60-65% of FY27 revenue is executable this year; about INR1,500 crores of revenue is available for FY28, excluding the pipeline and orders expected in the next six months.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify revenue deferred in Q2.
qa_highlights.answer: Around INR30-40 crores could not be dispatched due to logistics delays and rain.

qa_highlights.question: Timing and size of the Dangote/JNK Global balance order?
qa_highlights.answer: The current ~INR500 crore order covers supply only; balance scope (erection, commissioning, supervision) is under discussion and is a possibility, not certain, with timing in two to three months. Management said contract timelines start only on receipt of advance.

qa_highlights.question: Clarify the Nigeria heater count and remaining awards.
qa_highlights.answer: Three to four additional heaters beyond the nine in the current order are yet to be awarded; additional offers of about INR700-800 crores for Nigeria and fertiliser opportunities are in the pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Bid-to-win ratio and working capital funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Heater bid-to-win is about 30%; non-heater expected at 10-15%. No plan for additional debt; working capital to be funded from customer payment terms, reserves and bank limits.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material price risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel variation clauses exist in some PSU contracts; copper, nickel and aluminium are business risk, mitigated partly via back-to-back arrangements, hedging or pre-booking. Current projects not significantly affected.

risks_watch: Q2 execution slippage (INR30-40 crores deferred); H2 must deliver roughly 60-65% of FY27 revenue to meet guidance.
October and November progress described as weak, with recovery dependent on December-March.
Dangote/JNK Global balance order timing and size remain uncertain; management declined to confirm.
Non-heater diversification bid-to-win of only 10-15% expected; pipeline conversion timing may spill into Q1 FY28.
Commodity price volatility (copper, nickel, aluminium) on fixed-price contracts; geopolitical logistics risk.
Order disclosure granularity: management acknowledged the INR300-600 crore range was too wide and committed to narrower ranges.
summary.management_tone: Confident on full-year guidance and H2 recovery, but cautious and somewhat evasive on the size and timing of the JNK Global balance order and on pipeline conversion. Management repeatedly relied on the historical H2 weighting to explain H1 weakness.
key_quotes: Consequently, delays in shipment or site-level activities can have a bearing on the timing of revenue recognition.
Unless we have in the hand, we cannot say it is certain.
Whatever the balance 60%-65% of the revenue, it's easily executable in this year.
But as a policy, we do not want to give the exact order value for various reasons, as our client also do not want us to declare the exact value.

financial_highlights.value: INR5,000 crores (excluding recent JNK Global win)

growth.why: FY27 guidance of 20-25% revenue growth (midpoint 22.5%) held, backed by an INR1,662 crore order book (about INR1,500 crore carrying into FY28 is cited) and a ~INR500 crore Nigeria export order, but Q2 revenue grew only 3.4% on shipment and monsoon delays, and the H2-weighted delivery is unproven; no capacity additions or capex were discussed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 12-14% held vs H1 at 10.6% and Q2 at 11.1%, so H2 must lift margins, but no specific cost or mix lever was quantified and steel/copper/nickel/aluminium costs are a business risk.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Brief states no capex or capacity figures were discussed in the call.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-25% held; H1 already up 30.4% to INR370.2 crores, and 60-65% of FY27 revenue must be executed in H2 from a INR1,662 crore order book, though Q2 grew only 3.4% and INR30-40 crores slipped.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex or capacity discussed; utilisation not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was only maintained, not raised, while Q2 revenue grew 3.4% and October-November are expected to be slow with recovery only from December.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Guidance rests on H2 delivering 60-65% of FY27 revenue after INR30-40 crores of Q2 deferrals and weak Oct-Nov, and the Dangote balance order (~INR500 crores) is unconfirmed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product or model launches discussed; JNK Chemdist revenue expected only in about two years.

rows.label: Dangote/JNK Global balance scope (~INR500 crores)
rows.why: Balance scope (erection, commissioning, supervision) is under discussion but unconfirmed, and management said contract timelines start only on receipt of advance.

rows.label: Non-heater pipeline conversion (~INR1,500 crores to bid)
rows.when: next 1-2 quarters, may spill into Q1 FY28
rows.why: Expected bid-to-win is only 10-15%, against about 30% for heaters, so most of the ~INR2,500 crore non-heater opportunity is unlikely to convert soon.

rows.label: Kenya refinery and Nigeria additional awards
rows.why: Kenya inquiries expected in December, and three to four more Nigeria heaters plus INR700-800 crores of offers are in the pipeline, all still unawarded.

tone.note: Management was confident on full-year 20-25% revenue and 12-14% margin guidance and H2 weighting, but cautious and evasive on the size and timing of the Dangote/JNK Global balance order and on pipeline conversion; analysts pressed on how H2 can deliver after weak Q2.
